key_insight: A semi-smooth Newton reduced-order framework, augmented with neural corrections and hyper-reduction, can efficiently solve nonlinear parametric variational inequalities in solid mechanics.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster surrogate simulation of contact and obstacle-type mechanics problems while preserving the primal-dual structure needed for accurate constraint handling.
method: Build POD reduced bases for both primal and dual solution snapshots.
Add two feedforward networks to correct truncated POD coordinates and form a nonlinear manifold.
Use sparse-cubature hyper-reduction with greedy nonnegative least squares to cut online residual costs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical tests on a 2D obstacle problem and a 3D frictional contact problem, comparing full-order, linear reduced, neural-augmented, and hyper-reduced variants with substantial online cost reductions.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of snapshot training and on how well hyper-reduction preserves the nonlinear complementarity structure during Newton iterations.
paper_title: A Hyper-Reduced Neural Network-Augmented Semi-smooth Newton Method for Nonlinear Parametric Variational Inequalities
